case_description: Someone stole my mobile phone from my pocket in a crowded bus.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 34 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, I seek to institute a complaint against the perpetrator(s) for the alleged commission of the offence of 'dishonestly misappropriating property' under Article 265 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically Article 265(1)(b) read with Article 265(2).

Under Article 23 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, I request the registering of a First Information Report (FIR) and an investigation be initiated under Article 26(1) of the same Act.

Pursuant to Article 13 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, I seek to adduce evidence of the occurrence, including the fact that the mobile phone was in my possession prior to its alleged theft and that it was stolen during the commotion in the crowded bus.

case_description: A man entered my house at night by breaking the door and took my jewelry.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Investigation and Prosecution Pursuant to Article 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Article 17(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

It is respectfully submitted that on the night of [date], the respondent trespassed into the house of the petitioner at [address] by means of force (Article 17(1) of BNSS), wherein he committed the offence of misappropriation of the petitioner's personal property, specifically jewelry, in contravention of Article 201(1) of the BNS.

The petitioner humbly requests that an investigation be conducted under Article 123(2) of the BNS to identify the respondent and secure evidence of the said offence, and that the respondent be prosecuted in accordance with Article 17(1) of the BNSS and Article 201(1) of the BNS.

Supporting documents and evidence are attached hereto.

Please accept this petition as a formal complaint.

Respectfully submitted,
[Petitioner's Name]

case_description: My neighbor keeps threatening to beat me if I use the common parking area.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 228(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Section 3 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I seek to know whether my neighbor's statements, threatening to cause bodily harm to me if I use the common parking area, constitute an offence under the BNS and if so, what are the applicable provisions and remedies available to me.

case_description: Two people started fighting on the street and one hit the other with a stick causing injuries.
rephrased_query:
**Incident Report and Legal Query**

**Case Description:** On [date], two individuals engaged in a physical altercation on a public street, resulting in one party inflicting grievous bodily harm upon the other using a stick.

**Legal Query:**

Pursuant to Article 304 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the actions of the accused constitute an offense under Chapter 10, Section 3, 'Causing Death or Grievous Hurt by a Hazardous Substance or an Instrument' or Chapter 16, Section 6, 'Voluntarily Causing Hurt' of the BNS? 

Further, under the provisions of Article 215 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what is the appropriate course of action for the investigating officer to take in securing the scene, collecting evidence, and recording statements from witnesses?

Additionally, in light of Article 123 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), how do the circumstances of the incident affect the admissibility of the physical evidence collected, particularly the stick used to inflict harm, and any other relevant documentation or testimony?

case_description: A person sent me abusive and vulgar messages repeatedly on WhatsApp.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 5 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I respectfully seek your opinion on the following:

Whether the recipient of the abusive and vulgar messages has committed an offence under Article 12 of BNS, specifically Section 12(1)(a) - 'Malignant Communication', by sending repeated messages with intent to harm or harass the complainant, and whether this may be classified as a 'continuing offence' under Article 12(2) of BNS.

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I would like to inquire as to the procedure for lodging a complaint and obtaining necessary protection orders, specifically under Chapter VII - 'Protective Orders for Victims of Harassment and Malignant Communication', and whether a Magistrate's Order can be issued under Article 25(3) of BNSS.

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I would like to seek your opinion on the admissibility of WhatsApp messages as evidence, specifically under Article 21 - 'Digital Communication Evidence', and whether the messages will be considered relevant and reliable evidence in a court of law.

case_description: A person sent me abusive and vulgar messages repeatedly on WhatsApp.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 5, Section 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following formal legal query:

What constitutes a case of harassment under the provisions of BNS, specifically Article 15, Section 4, in relation to an individual sending repetitive abusive and vulgar messages on a digital platform, such as WhatsApp, and what penalties or remedies are available to the aggrieved party under BNSS, specifically Article 27, Section 6, for the commission of such offense?

case_description: Someone forged my signature on a cheque and withdrew money from my account.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Section 420 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), which deals with Cheating and Breach of Trust, I seek clarification on whether an offence under BNS has been committed by an individual who forged the signature on a cheque issued by me, thereby facilitating the withdrawal of funds from my account, thereby causing me financial loss.

Furthermore, under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and Article 110, I request guidance on the necessary procedures and protocols to be followed to lodge a complaint, investigate the case, and ensure the apprehension and prosecution of the perpetrator, as well as compensation for the damages suffered by me.

Additionally, under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I seek to understand the admissibility and relevance of the forged cheque as evidence in the trial, specifically under Article 32, which deals with the Proof of Signature.

Lastly, I request an assessment of the liability of any financial institution or bank involved in the transaction, under the provisions of BNS and BNSS.

case_description: My landlord locked me out of my rented room without any notice and kept my belongings inside.
rephrased_query:
Query:

Pursuant to Article 34, Clause 2 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), has the landlord committed the offence of wrongful confinement or illegal detention under Article 42, Section 1 of BNS, by locking out the tenant from the rented premises without lawful notice, thereby rendering the tenant unable to access their personal belongings as mentioned under Article 19, Section 5 of BNS? 

Additionally, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what procedures can be initiated under Chapter 3, Article 7, to secure the release of the tenant's belongings and ensure the landlord's compliance with the relevant laws?

case_description: A group of people damaged my shop during a protest by throwing stones and breaking the glass.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 43 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I submit the following formal complaint for consideration:

Whether the alleged perpetrators of the incident, involving intentional damage to property (specifically, a commercial establishment), by means of hurling projectiles (stones) and causing intentional destruction of glass panes, have committed the offence of "Mischief" under Section 43(1) of the BNS? 

Additionally, I request an investigation into the circumstances surrounding this incident, as mandated by Section 23 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), with a view to determining whether the perpetrators were acting in contravention of Sections 13 and 14 of the BNSS, which pertain to the maintenance of public order and the prevention of unlawful assemblies.

Furthermore, I seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in relation to the identification of the perpetrators and the reconstruction of the events surrounding the incident, in light of Article 17(2) of the BSA, which deals with the admissibility of circumstantial evidence.

case_description: A stranger keeps calling and sending messages threatening to burn my shop if I do not pay him money.
rephrased_query:
Application of Section 306 of BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023) for alleged offences under Section 506 of BNS, seeking redress under Section 155 of BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) for protection and investigation.

Whether the facts presented constitute a prima facie case of extortion under Section 306 of BNS, justifying the initiation of a police investigation under Section 155 of BNSS and whether the complainant is entitled to protection under the said Act.

Further, this application seeks clarification on the admissibility of electronic evidence, including voice messages and SMS, as per Article 59 of BSA (Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023) for purposes of prosecution under Section 306 of BNS.

case_description: Someone hacked my social media account and posted offensive content using my name.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Relief under Article 39(1)(b) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS): 

Complainant seeks immediate action against the perpetrator who, with malicious intent, committed an act of cybercrime by hacking into the complainant's social media account and posting content deemed offensive under Article 11(6) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). Prayer is made for the registration of an FIR as per Article 23(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and for necessary investigation under Article 46(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Further, this petition seeks the exclusion of the offending content as evidence under Article 56(2) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) and any other relief deemed fit and necessary by the court to protect the complainant's reputation and ensure the perpetrator's accountability for their actions.

Request is made under Article 5(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the court to expedite this matter and ensure fair and just treatment of the complainant.

case_description: Someone hacked my social media account and posted offensive content using my name.
rephrased_query:
Complaint against Unauthorised Use of Personal Information and Defamation under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 123 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek your assistance in filing a complaint against an individual who has committed the offence of unauthorised use of personal information under Article 234(1)(a) of BNS, whereby my social media account was accessed without my consent, and offensive content was posted using my name.

Furthermore, under Article 219 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I also seek to file a complaint against the said individual for the offence of defamation, as the said content has caused harm to my reputation and goodwill.

Under Section 53(4) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I request that the investigation be conducted expeditiously, and the accused be brought to justice.

Pursuant to Article 17 of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), I submit the following documents as evidence:

* Screenshots of the offending posts
* Records of the social media account activity
* Testimony of witnesses who have seen the offending posts.

I request that the authorities take immediate action in this matter, investigate the circumstances surrounding the unauthorised use of my personal information and the posting of defamatory content, and bring the accused to justice in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS).

case_description: During a land dispute my uncle stabbed my father multiple times with a knife and he died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 226 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I seek guidance on the applicable provisions in the event of a homicide committed during a dispute over immovable property.

Specifically, I would like to know whether the circumstances of the incident, wherein my uncle allegedly stabbed my father multiple times with a sharp-edged object, resulting in his instantaneous demise, would attract the charges of murder under Article 312 of the BNS.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what is the procedure for registering a First Information Report (FIR) and commencing an investigation in this case, particularly considering the fact that the dispute was related to immovable property and the accused is a family member?

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what is the admissible evidence that can be used to establish the guilt of the accused, taking into account the testimony of witnesses, any physical evidence collected from the crime scene, and any other relevant facts and circumstances of the case?

case_description: During a land dispute my uncle stabbed my father multiple times with a knife and he died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To whom it may concern,

I, [Your Name], son of the deceased, hereby lodge a complaint against my uncle, [Uncle's Name], for the alleged commission of the offence under BNS, Section 302 - Murder.

**Particulars of the Offence:**

On [date], at [place], my uncle, [Uncle's Name], with intent to kill, caused grievous hurt to my father by stabbing him multiple times with a knife. As a direct result of these injuries, my father succumbed to his injuries on the spot.

**Request for Investigation and Prosecution:**

I request that a thorough investigation be conducted under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and that my uncle be apprehended and prosecuted for the said offence. I also request that the evidence, including medical and forensic reports, be collected and preserved in accordance with the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

**Signature:**
[Your Signature]

**Date:**
[Date]

Please note that this is a formal complaint and may be used as evidence in any subsequent legal proceedings.

case_description: A man poured acid on a woman's face after she rejected his marriage proposal and she later succumbed to injuries.
rephrased_query:
In view of the above circumstances, a formal complaint is sought to be filed under Section 302 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the alleged commission of the offence of Murder. 

Further, it is desired to seek an order under Article 176 of the BNSS to conduct an inquest into the cause of death of the deceased, in order to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Additionally, it is requested to direct the collection of evidence, including forensic reports, under Section 65 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) to determine the extent of the injuries caused to the deceased and to establish the culpability of the accused.

It is also prayed that the accused be charged under Section 317 of BNS for the offence of voluntarily causing grievous hurt by means of poison, corrosive substance or hot substance, as the accused allegedly poured acid on the victim's face.

Furthermore, it is sought to invoke the provisions of Section 188 of BNSS to obtain an order of protection for the family of the deceased, in light of the sensitive nature of the case.

case_description: A man poured acid on a woman's face after she rejected his marriage proposal and she later succumbed to injuries.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), an inquiry is required to determine whether the accused has committed the offence of causing grievous hurt by an offender by means of poison, etc. (Article 315, BNS) and whether the said act was motivated by the victim's rejection of the accused's marriage proposal, thereby constituting the offence of dowry harassment or harassment with intent to coerce (Article 322, BNS).

Furthermore, an investigation is needed to ascertain whether the accused has committed the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, punishable under Article 302, BNS, and whether the victim's death was a direct consequence of the injuries inflicted upon her.

Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the inquiry and investigation should be conducted in accordance with the provisions related to the investigation of cognizable offences (Chapter VII, BNSS) and the provisions related to the investigation of non-cognizable offences (Chapter VIII, BNSS).

During the inquiry and investigation, the admissibility of evidence and the burden of proof should be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), specifically Article 21(1)(d), BSA, which deals with the burden of proof and the standard of proof in criminal cases.

case_description: My neighbor hit my brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument; he is in ICU and may not survive.
rephrased_query:
PETITION UNDER THE BHARATIYA NYAYA SANHITA 2023 (BNS) FOR REGISTRATION OF AN OFFENCE AND GRANT OF PROTECTION ORDERS:

To the Magistrate of the First Class,

I, [Your Name], submit this petition stating that my brother, [Brother's Name], is a victim of a grievous hurt inflicted by my neighbor, [Neighbor's Name], who on [Date of Incident], in a fit of rage, struck my brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument. My brother is currently admitted in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of [Hospital Name] and is in a precarious condition, with a high likelihood of succumbing to his injuries.

Pursuant to BNS, Article 13 (a) -  'Causing grievous hurt', I request that a First Information Report (FIR) be registered against [Neighbor's Name] under the aforesaid provision, and that necessary legal proceedings be initiated against him.

Furthermore, I pray for protection orders under BNS, Article 21 (c) - 'Protection from harassment and intimidation' as well as under BNSS, Section 154 (1) - 'Duty of the Magistrate to cause an inquiry into the cause of death or grievous hurt', to ensure that my family and I are not harassed or intimidated by the accused or any of his associates during the pendency of these proceedings.

I request that this petition be considered and necessary action be taken at the earliest.

Respectfully submitted,

[Your Name]

case_description: My neighbor hit my brother on the head with an iron rod during a heated argument; he is in ICU and may not survive.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, a complaint is hereby filed under the provisions of Section 299, BNS, read with Section 302, BNS, regarding an alleged offence of "Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder" (Section 306, BNS) and "Murder" (Section 307, BNS), committed by the neighbour against the brother. 

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, an application is made under Section 154, BNSS, to register an FIR (First Information Report) in this regard and to initiate an investigation into the said incident. 

Additionally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, we seek guidance on the admissibility of evidence in this case, specifically with regards to the provisions of Section 59, BSA, regarding the admissibility of statements made by the injured party (the brother) prior to his hospitalization, and Section 60, BSA, regarding the admissibility of medical evidence, including the hospital records of the brother.

case_description: Two men got into a drunken fight and one pushed the other off a bridge, causing his death.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), is the accused liable to be charged under Section 302 of BNS, "Murder", for causing the death of the deceased individual, considering the act of being pushed off a bridge as an act of commission with intent to cause grievous bodily harm, culminating in the deceased's demise?

Furthermore, with respect to the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the query seeks clarification on the procedural aspects, specifically the process for registering an FIR, conducting an investigation, and obtaining necessary permissions for the post-mortem examination under Article 176 of BNSS.

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), is the prosecution required to establish the accused's intent to cause harm, and what is the standard of proof required to establish the culpability of the accused under Section 52 of BSA, "Presumption as to culpable homicide"?

case_description: Two men got into a drunken fight and one pushed the other off a bridge, causing his death.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Section 306 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

In the matter of the untimely demise of [Name of the deceased], who lost his life due to alleged culpable homicide, we seek clarification on the applicability of BNS Section 306, which pertains to culpable homicide not amounting to murder, particularly in scenarios involving reckless or negligent conduct. Specifically, we wish to understand whether the actions of the accused individual, who, in a state of intoxication, pushed the deceased off a bridge, resulting in his fatal fall, would constitute an offense under BNS Section 306.

Additionally, we request guidance on the procedural aspects of this matter, including the filing of the complaint, the initiation of an investigation, and the subsequent legal proceedings under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically Article 167, which deals with the procedure for investigating cognizable offenses.

Furthermore, we seek clarification on the admissibility of evidence under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with regard to the testimony of witnesses, the admissibility of statements made by the accused during the investigation, and the role of circumstantial evidence in establishing the guilt of the accused.

We kindly request the court's guidance on these matters, in order to ensure a thorough and fair investigation into the circumstances surrounding the deceased's untimely demise.

case_description: A bus driver was driving recklessly at high speed and ran over a pedestrian who died on the spot.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 226 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is sought to be registered against the bus driver for the alleged commission of the offence under Section 302 of the BNS, read with Section 279 of the BNS, for causing the death of a pedestrian by rash and negligent driving. 

The specific circumstances of the incident are as follows:

- The bus driver was driving at a high speed in a reckless manner.
- The bus driver collided with a pedestrian, resulting in the pedestrian's death on the spot.
- The bus driver has allegedly failed to exercise due care and caution while driving the vehicle, thereby endangering the life or personal safety of others.

It is requested that the investigating officer be directed to register a case under Section 302 of the BNS and Section 279 of the BNS, and to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident, taking into account the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) dealing with the collection and preservation of evidence, as well as the examination and cross-examination of witnesses, in accordance with the provisions of Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

case_description: A bus driver was driving recklessly at high speed and ran over a pedestrian who died on the spot.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 45 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), in relation to Article 27, I request clarification on the liability of the bus driver under the provisions of 'Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder' for causing the death of the pedestrian, arising out of his alleged 'Reckless Driving' in contravention of Article 32 of the BNS, and whether the offense falls within the definition of 'Cognizable Offense' as per Article 56 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), thus necessitating registration of a First Information Report (FIR) under Article 20 of the BNSS.

case_description: A wife was continuously tortured by her husband and in-laws for dowry; she was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Investigation and Potential Prosecution under Section 304B of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Section 176 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

To the Hon'ble Magistrate of the District Court,

Pursuant to the alleged incident of a female individual being found hanging in her room within a span of two years of her marriage, there is a reasonable suspicion of her having been subjected to cruelty and harassment by her husband and in-laws for dowry. It is requested that an investigation be conducted under Article 21 of the Constitution of India and Section 176 of the BNSS to determine the circumstances surrounding the deceased's death.

It is respectfully prayed that:

1. A magisterial inquiry be conducted to gather evidence and interview relevant witnesses, as per Section 176 of the BNSS.
2. The investigation be carried out with due diligence and promptness to ensure that the rights of the deceased and her family are protected.
3. The findings of the investigation be submitted to this Hon'ble Court for further proceedings, if warranted.
4. In the event that the investigation reveals sufficient evidence, criminal proceedings be initiated against the accused under Section 304B of the BNS, which deals with dowry-related deaths.

Prayer for a fair and impartial investigation, and for such further orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit.

Respectfully submitted,
[Your Name]

Advocate for the Petitioner.

case_description: A wife was continuously tortured by her husband and in-laws for dowry; she was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage.
rephrased_query:
Subject: Query regarding alleged commission of offence under BNS, 2023 - Suicidal Death of Spouse

Respected Hon'ble Magistrate/Judge,

I seek your esteemed guidance on the following matter:

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 302 of the BNS, 2023, I would like to inquire about the applicability of the offence of Dowry Harassment as defined under Article 498 (2) and (3) of the BNS, 2023, in the following scenario:

A married woman (hereinafter referred to as the "deceased") was subjected to continuous harassment and torture by her husband and his family members (hereinafter referred to as the "accused") for dowry within a period of two years from the date of marriage. The deceased was found deceased, allegedly by hanging, in her room on a certain date.

In light of the aforesaid circumstances, I kindly request Your Honour to clarify whether the accused can be held liable under Article 498 (2) and (3) of the BNS, 2023, for the alleged commission of the offence.

Additionally, I would like to seek Your Honour's guidance on the procedure to be followed under the BNSS, 2023, for registering an FIR (First Information Report) and conducting an investigation into this matter.

Furthermore, I would appreciate Your Honour's clarification on the admissibility of evidence under the BSA, 2023, and the burden of proof that would lie on the prosecution in establishing the guilt of the accused.

I look forward to receiving Your Honour's guidance and assistance in this matter.

Respectfully submitted,

[Your Name]

case_description: A wife was continuously tortured by her husband and in-laws for dowry; she was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage.
rephrased_query:
**INQUIRY INTO CIRCUMSTANCES SURROUNDING THE DEATH OF A FEMALE**

Pursuant to Section 176(1)(g) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), a complaint is made against the husband and in-laws of the deceased for alleged commission of the offence under Section 312(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), read with Sections 312(2) and 312(3) thereof, arising out of the continuous harassment and torture inflicted upon the deceased by the accused.

The circumstances of the case, including the fact that the deceased was found hanging in her room within two years of marriage, necessitate an investigation to ascertain whether the death was caused by the accused's acts constituting the aforesaid offence.

The prosecution is required to prove the guilt of the accused under Section 101(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), which provides that the burden of proving the defence of the accused lies on them. Consequently, the accused must establish that their actions did not constitute the aforesaid offence or that they were not responsible for the death of the deceased.

The court is required to inquire into the circumstances surrounding the death and to determine whether the accused are guilty of the offence alleged against them, in accordance with the principles of natural justice and the provisions of the BNSS and the BNS.

case_description: A teenager posted on social media encouraging her classmate to commit suicide; the classmate later took her own life.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a complaint is sought to be registered against the teenager under Article 320 (1) ('Abetment of suicide') and Article 321 (1) ('Causing death by abetment') for allegedly inducing her classmate to commit suicide through a social media post, which ultimately led to the classmate's death.

The facts of the case necessitate an investigation under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), specifically Section 94 (1) ('Preliminary inquiry by Magistrate'), to determine whether sufficient grounds exist to warrant a trial. During the course of the investigation, the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) shall apply, particularly Section 42 (3) ('Presumption as to abetment of suicide'), to guide the assessment of evidence and the establishment of the requisite causation in support of the charges.

The complainant shall be required to provide the investigation agency with relevant proof and evidence under Article 54 (1) ('Burden of proof') of the BSA, to substantiate the allegations of abetment and causation.

case_description: A teenager posted on social media encouraging her classmate to commit suicide; the classmate later took her own life.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Investigation and Prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

To the Honourable Magistrate,

Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I submit this petition for investigation and prosecution of the following offence:

The petitioner's daughter, a minor, allegedly posted a message on social media encouraging her classmate to take her own life, which ultimately led to the classmate's demise. This act may be considered an abetment to suicide under Article 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), as it appears to have instigated the classmate to take her own life.

Please consider initiating a magisterial inquiry under Section 19(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to investigate the said incident and determine the culpability of the petitioner's daughter. Furthermore, if found guilty, the petitioner seeks prosecution under Article 305 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for abetment to suicide.

The petitioner requests the Honourable Magistrate to expedite the inquiry and prosecution process under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).

Respectfully submitted,

[Your Name]

case_description: A teenager posted on social media encouraging her classmate to commit suicide; the classmate later took her own life.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)**

**Query:** A case is reported where a minor, vide a social media post, allegedly incited her classmate to take her own life, which subsequently led to the classmate's demise. 

**Question:**

1. **Offence under BNS:** Can the minor be held liable for abetment of suicide under Article 302(1)(a) of BNS, given that her actions allegedly led to the classmate's death? 
2. **Investigation under BNSS:** What provisions of BNSS (Articles 54, 55, and 56) govern the investigation into this incident, particularly in relation to the minor's social media post and its probable impact on the classmate?
3. **Evidence collection under BSA:** What sections of BSA (Articles 17, 28, 29, and 31) would be applicable in collecting and preserving evidence related to the social media post, online activities, and other relevant data in this case?
4. **Proceedings and Trial under BNSS:** What is the procedure under BNSS (Articles 80, 81, and 82) for conducting the trial, considering the minor's age, and ensuring that justice is served in a fair and compassionate manner?

**Request:** In light of BNS, BNSS, and BSA, kindly provide guidance on the applicable laws, procedures, and any relevant precedents that may be cited in this case.

case_description: A life-convict on parole got into a fight and strangled another person to death.

Pursuant to Article 43 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the act of abandoning a newborn infant (as defined under Article 12 of BNS) by a mother in a public place (as defined under Article 15 of BNS) near a hospital constitutes the offence of 'Neglect of a Child' or any other applicable provision under Chapter 3 of BNS.

Additionally, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what are the applicable procedures for the investigation, collection of evidence, and subsequent arrest, if any, of the mother in light of this incident?

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what are the admissibility and relevance of the following evidence in the context of this case: eyewitness testimony, CCTV footage, and any other circumstantial evidence that may be collected.

case_description: A begging ring operator hired several children aged 7-10 to beg at traffic signals and took all the money they collected.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, Section 4(1)(a) (Definition of Culpable Homicide and other Offences), what are the penal consequences and legal liabilities under Article 5(2)(a) for the offence of child trafficking and forced begging as defined under Article 8(1)(c) and Article 8(1)(d) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, read with Article 10(1)(b) and Article 11(3)(a) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023?

Further, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, what are the procedural steps and legal remedies available under Article 17(3)(c) and Article 20(2)(d) for the protection and rehabilitation of the trafficked children, and what are the legal obligations of the investigating officer under Article 28(1)(f) and Article 30(4)(a) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023?

case_description: A begging ring operator hired several children aged 7-10 to beg at traffic signals and took all the money they collected.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 294, Chapter III, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Offences relating to the breach of public peace), and Article 321, Chapter XIII, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Offences by or relating to children), we seek clarification on the liability of the begging ring operator in relation to the criminal offence of:

 Article 294, Chapter III, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023: Does the act of coercing and employing children in begging, thereby causing disturbance to public peace, constitute an offence under this provision?

 Article 321, Chapter XIII, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023: What is the legal status of the children involved in this begging ring, and are they entitled to protection under this provision?

Furthermore, under Article 23(1), Chapter II, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (Trafficking), we seek to understand whether the recruitment and employment of children in begging constitutes human trafficking, and if so, the applicable penalties and procedures under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023.

Additionally, under Article 15, Chapter I, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (Relevancy and burden of proof), we seek guidance on the evidentiary requirements to establish the guilt of the begging ring operator and the liability of the children involved.

case_description: A begging ring operator hired several children aged 7-10 to beg at traffic signals and took all the money they collected.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested to determine whether the accused has committed the offence under Section 4(1)(iii) of BNS, read with Article 8(5) thereof, which pertains to the exploitation of a minor through forced labour or begging. 

Further, under the BNSS 2023, it is sought to know whether the accused can be arrested under Article 73(1) of BNSS, in the absence of the complainant or informant, as the offence under Section 4(1)(iii) of BNS is a cognizable offence, as per Article 5(2) of BNSS.

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is requested to establish whether the testimony of the minor victims is admissible in evidence under Article 27(3) of BSA, despite the fact that they are below the age of 12, and whether the collected evidence is sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused under Article 31(4) of BSA.

case_description: A couple secretly delivered a baby and disposed of the body to conceal the birth from neighbours.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 320 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), the following query is posed:

Whether the acts of the couple, in secretly concealing the birth and disposing of the body, amount to an offence under Section 305 of BNS, specifically with regard to the omission to give information regarding the birth, and, if so, do the provisions of Section 306 of BNS apply, thereby rendering the couple liable for culpable homicide not amounting to murder?

Furthermore, under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what are the procedural requirements and powers of the authorities to investigate and prosecute this alleged offence, particularly with regard to Sections 154, 157, and 173 of BNSS? 

Additionally, under Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what is the admissibility and relevancy of evidence, including any circumstantial evidence, in proving the alleged offence, specifically with regard to Sections 3, 6, and 45 of BSA?

case_description: A couple secretly delivered a baby and disposed of the body to conceal the birth from neighbours.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is respectfully submitted that a criminal inquiry be initiated under Section 313 (1) of BNS against the couple for the alleged commission of a criminal offense.

Specifically, the query seeks clarification on the applicability of Section 313 (1) BNS regarding the concealment of birth against the couple, who have been accused of secretly delivering a baby and disposing of the body to conceal the birth from their neighbours.

Further, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the couple's actions may also be investigated under Article 22 (4) of BNSS for alleged non-compliance with the mandatory reporting requirements for births and deaths, as mandated under the law.

Additionally, the admissibility of evidence in this case may be determined under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with respect to the application of Article 47 (2) BSA regarding the admissibility of circumstantial evidence in cases involving concealment of birth and disposition of human remains.

case_description: A couple secretly delivered a baby and disposed of the body to conceal the birth from neighbours.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 234(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), a query is raised regarding the criminal liability of the couple for the commission of the offence under Article 179(2), BNS, specifically the concealment and disposal of a newborn infant's body, thereby allegedly causing the said infant's death. 

In the context of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), the query seeks to determine whether the couple's actions constitute a cognizable offence under BNSS, thereby necessitating police investigation and prosecution under Article 41, BNSS.

case_description: A minor girl aged 14 was procured by a broker and supplied to a client for sexual exploitation.
rephrased_query:
Petition under Section 4(2)(a) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), seeking redressal for the alleged commission of a cognizable offence under Section 3(1)(i) of BNS, read with Article 15, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), for the issuance of a search warrant and arrest of the accused broker and client. 

Additionally, under Article 23 of BNSS, the petition seeks the protection and safeguarding of the minor victim, who is likely to be a 'child in need of care and protection' under Section 2(3) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), and the collection of evidence as per Article 28 of BSA, to establish the chain of procurement, supply, and exploitation of the minor victim.

case_description: A minor girl aged 14 was procured by a broker and supplied to a client for sexual exploitation.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Section 4(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Section 20 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), and Article 14 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), is the procurement of a minor girl by a broker and subsequent supply to a client for sexual exploitation punishable under BNS, and what are the requisite procedures for the registering of an FIR and subsequent investigation, as outlined in BNSS?

case_description: A minor girl aged 14 was procured by a broker and supplied to a client for sexual exploitation.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 123, Clause (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek an interpretation of the provision of 'procuring a child for illicit sexual intercourse', which, as per the facts, involves a 14-year-old minor girl. 

We request clarification on the nature of liability under BNS that may be applicable to the broker and the client involved in this alleged incident.

Furthermore, in relation to the procedure to be followed under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), we would like to know the steps that should be taken to protect the minor girl and ensure her safety, as well as the powers of the authorities to investigate and gather evidence in accordance with Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

case_description: A doctor performed an abortion on a woman in her eighth month of pregnancy without medical justification, and the baby died.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), it is requested that the following legal query be considered:

Whether the actions of the doctor, as described, constitute an offence under Article 226 of BNS, which pertains to 'Abortion not justified by medical indication', and, if so, whether the doctor can be held liable for the loss of life of the unborn child, in light of the principles enshrined under Article 123 of BNS, specifically addressing 'Liability for act done without legal justification'.

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), it is requested that the following query be addressed:

What are the procedural steps that would be applicable in this scenario, under BNSS, specifically with regard to the investigation and prosecution of the doctor, including the provisions for summons and warrants as may be necessary, as stipulated in BNSS Article 456, and the rights of the accused as enshrined under BNSS Article 675.

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), it is requested that the following query be considered:

What is the admissibility of evidence in this scenario, specifically with regard to the medical records and testimony of the doctor, under BSA Article 189, which pertains to the admissibility of medical records, and BSA Article 456, which addresses the credibility of expert witnesses, including medical professionals.

case_description: A doctor performed an abortion on a woman in her eighth month of pregnancy without medical justification, and the baby died.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the BNS, it is requested to determine whether the doctor has committed an offence under Section 322 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, punishable under Article 13, by causing the death of a foetus beyond 12 weeks of gestation, when no medical necessity necessitated the termination of pregnancy, thereby violating the provisions of Article 16. 

Additionally, under the BNSS, please consider the admissibility of the medical records and testimony of the doctor and the woman as evidence under Chapter VII, particularly Article 28, in relation to the investigation of this incident. 

Furthermore, the relevant provisions of the BSA, specifically Article 45, should be applied to determine the admissibility of expert medical testimony in this case, in relation to the standard of medical care and the justification for the abortion.

case_description: A doctor performed an abortion on a woman in her eighth month of pregnancy without medical justification, and the baby died.
rephrased_query: Whether the doctor's actions constitute an offence under Article 312 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), specifically Section 1(d) of Article 312, and if so, whether the prosecution can proceed under Section 19(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), considering the principles of causation and liability as enunciated under Article 45 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA) in assessing the doctor's culpability for the baby's death.

case_description: A woman was forcibly given medicine by her mother-in-law to cause a miscarriage because the family wanted a boy child.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Investigation and Action under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

Whether the actions of the mother-in-law, involving the administration of medicine with the intention of causing a miscarriage, amount to an offence under Article 221 of BNS, specifically the offence of "Causing or attempting to cause miscarriage" and/or Article 245 of BNS, "Cruelty by husband or relatives"? 

Facts of the case: The mother-in-law administered medicine with the intention of causing a miscarriage, resulting in harm to the pregnant woman, at the instigation of the family who wanted a male child. 

Prayer: We pray that an investigation be initiated under Article 22 of BNSS, and the accused be apprehended and prosecuted for the said offences. 

Whether the woman's right to life, personal liberty, and dignity has been violated under Articles 15 and 21 of the Constitution of India? 

Whether the family's actions and intentions amount to a conspiracy under Article 248 of BNS, and if so, whether they can be held liable for the said offences? 

We pray that the court may grant such other relief as may be deemed fit and proper in the circumstances of the case.

case_description: A woman was forcibly given medicine by her mother-in-law to cause a miscarriage because the family wanted a boy child.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Relief:

I, the undersigned, hereby request your esteemed consideration to the following matter:

Can a complaint be filed under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) for the offence of intentionally causing a miscarriage without the woman's consent (Section 316 of BNS), as allegedly committed by the mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, thereby amounting to an act of dowry harassment and/or cruelty by the family in pursuit of their preference for a male child, thus violating the provisions of Article 15 of the Constitution of India and/or the rights of the woman guaranteed under the provisions of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005?

Furthermore, can the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) be invoked to grant protection to the complainant under the circumstances of this case, considering the potential threat to her life and well-being posed by the family members?

Additionally, can the admissibility of evidence in this matter be determined in light of the provisions of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), particularly with regard to the admissibility of medical records, statements of witnesses, and other relevant documentation that may be crucial to establishing the facts of this case?

Your attention to this matter is respectfully solicited.

case_description: A woman was forcibly given medicine by her mother-in-law to cause a miscarriage because the family wanted a boy child.
rephrased_query:
**Complaint/Information under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To: The Officer-in-Charge of the concerned Police Station,

I hereby lodge a complaint/report an incident of causing harm to a pregnant woman by administering a substance (medicine), allegedly to induce a miscarriage, under Section 319(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS). The accused, being the mother-in-law of the complainant (wife of the complainant's husband), is alleged to have acted with intent to terminate the pregnancy, contrary to the principles of personal liberty and the rights of the complainant as enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution.

**Specifically, the complaint alleges:**

*   Administration of a substance to cause harm to the complainant's unborn child without her consent or knowledge, which amounts to an act of violence against the complainant and her unborn child.

**Prayer:**

*   Registration of an FIR under Section 319(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) against the accused mother-in-law.
*   Investigation into the incident to establish the facts and identify the accused individuals responsible for this incident.
*   Prophylactic measures to prevent further harm to the complainant and her unborn child.

**Verification:**

I hereby verify that the facts stated in this complaint are true to the best of my knowledge. I request the police to conduct a thorough investigation and take necessary action as per the law.

**Declaration:**

I declare that I have submitted this complaint voluntarily and without any undue influence or coercion.

Signature of the Complainant

case_description: A 5-year-old child was enticed with chocolates by a neighbour who then kept the child locked in his house for two days.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to BNS, 2023, it is requested to enquire into the commission of the offence described as 'Child Trafficking' under Article 321 (a), BNS, 2023, wherein an individual, acting in a manner as described, allegedly enticed a child with an offer of sweets and subsequently confined the child in a dwelling, thereby depriving the child of liberty.

Further, under BNSS, 2023, it is requested to investigate the said incident and determine whether the said individual has committed the offence of 'Custodial Crime' under Section 37 (1) of BNSS, 2023, which entails the confinement of a person without their consent.

Additionally, under BSA, 2023, it is requested to assess the admissibility of the child's statement as evidence, which may be obtained under the provisions of Section 18 (1) of BSA, 2023, regarding the statements of vulnerable persons, and to examine whether the neighbour's act of offering sweets to the child can be considered as an inducement under Article 19 (b) of BSA, 2023.

case_description: A 5-year-old child was enticed with chocolates by a neighbour who then kept the child locked in his house for two days.
rephrased_query:
PETITION FOR INVESTIGATION AND PROSECUTION UNDER THE BHARATIYA NYAYA SANHITA 2023 (BNS)

To the Honourable Magistrate under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS),

I respectfully submit that an offence has been allegedly committed by [Neighbour's Name], a resident of [Neighbour's Address], under Article 34(1)(a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), which pertains to "Enticement of minor" by means of offering 'chocolates' or any other object of value.

It is further alleged that the said [Neighbour's Name] did, on [Date], at [Time] at his house, unlawfully confine the minor child, [Child's Name], aged 5 years, against their will, contrary to Article 44(2)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), which deals with "Detention of a person against their will".

case_description: A group posted online manifestos calling people to take up arms against the Indian government.
rephrased_query: Pursuant to Article 13 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), whether the act of posting online manifestos calling people to take up arms against the Indian government constitutes an act of sedition punishable under the provisions of BNS and/or contravenes any of the obligations or duties specified under Article 14(1)(a) of BNS, warranting an investigation and possible prosecution under the relevant sections of BNSS and/or BSA.

case_description: During a village election, a candidate distributed cash and liquor to voters to get their votes.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, Article 123(1) is it not an offence, punishable under Section 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, for a candidate to offer or promise, directly or indirectly, any gift or gratification to a voter, including cash and liquor, to influence the voter's decision in a village election?

Further, pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, Article 129(1) is it not a cognizable offence, under Section 129(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, to be taken cognizance of by an officer-in-charge of a police station, without a warrant, where a complaint is made that an offence under Section 123(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 has been committed in a village election?

Additionally, pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, Article 145(1) may the evidence of voters, who received gifts or gratifications from the candidate, be admissible, under Section 145(2) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, to prove the guilt of the candidate in a village election?

case_description: During a village election, a candidate distributed cash and liquor to voters to get their votes.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, whether the actions of the candidate constitutes an offence under Article 123(1)(a) of the BNS, specifically the act of offering or accepting any gratification for the purpose of influencing the outcome of an election, and whether the same can be termed as "illegitimate gratification" as mentioned under Article 123(4) of the BNS.

Further inquiring whether the distribution of liquor is in contravention to the provisions of Article 145(2) of the BNS, which prohibits the offering or giving of intoxicating liquor or any other intoxicating substance to any person with intent to induce that person to vote for any candidate or to influence the voting behavior of such person.

Additionally, seeking guidance under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, whether the candidate's actions can be treated as a cognizable offence and whether the election officer or any other authority can register an FIR under the BNSS in this regard.

Lastly, inquiring whether the evidence collected in this case, including the testimony of the voters and any documentary evidence of the distribution of cash and liquor, can be considered admissible under the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically Article 12(3) of the BSA, which deals with the admissibility of electronic evidence.

case_description: During a village election, a candidate distributed cash and liquor to voters to get their votes.
rephrased_query: What are the relevant provisions under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) that pertain to the distribution of cash and liquor to voters as an inducement to influence the outcome of the village election, specifically with regard to the crimes of bribery and electoral malpractices?

case_description: A mob of about 200 people armed with sticks and swords attacked shops belonging to a particular community after a rumour spread on social media.

Is the mob's attack on shops belonging to a particular community a punishable act under BNS, Article 121(1)(a)(iii) ('unlawful assembly' causing damage to property, thereby endangering the life or personal liberty of the victims)? Should the perpetrators be held liable for the commission of a cognizable offence under BNS, Article 153(2)(a) ('rioting', involving ten or more persons armed with deadly weapons, thereby causing harm to persons and property)? 

Furthermore, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), what is the admissibility of digital evidence (social media posts) in establishing the causal link between the rumour and the subsequent violence, particularly under BSA, Article 34(1)(d) ('circumstantial evidence')?

Lastly, under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), what is the procedure for registration of an FIR and subsequent investigation into the cognizable offence, as per BNSS, Article 50(3)(a) ('offence involving public disorder, rioting, or affray')?

case_description: A man voted in the election using someone else's identity card and later the real voter was turned away at the booth.
rephrased_query:
Petition for Criminal Prosecution under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS) and Inquiry under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS):

To the Honorable Magistrate,

This petition seeks to initiate a criminal investigation against the perpetrator who, on a date to be determined, committed the offence of 'Personation at an Election' under Article 120 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), by presenting another person's identity document to gain entry to vote in an election, and thereafter, causing harm or obstruction to the legitimate voter who was turned away at the booth in violation of Article 123 of the BNS.

I humbly request that the Magistrate, under the powers vested under Article 205 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), direct the police to conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and gather evidence, including witness statements, documents, and any other relevant material, in accordance with the provisions of Chapter VII of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

Please direct the police to collect all relevant evidence, including any CCTV footage or digital records, as well as to identify and record the statements of all witnesses who may have observed the incident, in order to determine the guilt or innocence of the perpetrator and to bring the perpetrators to justice.

case_description: A man voted in the election using someone else's identity card and later the real voter was turned away at the booth.
rephrased_query:

To the Hon'ble Magistrate and the Investigating Officer,

Furthermore, has the alleged offender violated Article 56(1)(c) of the BNSS (Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023) by committing an act which is likely to cause a breach of peace, and does this require an immediate investigation under Article 56(2) BNSS to ascertain the facts of the case?

Pursuant to Article 12(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), please provide the necessary guidance on the admissibility of evidence in this case, specifically in relation to the identity card used by the alleged offender, and whether the testimony of the real voter is admissible as primary evidence under Article 12(2) BSA.

Please provide a written response to this query at the earliest, stating the next course of action to be taken in this matter.

Yours faithfully,
[Your Name]

case_description: A man voted in the election using someone else's identity card and later the real voter was turned away at the booth.
rephrased_query:
Pursuant to the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), I pose the following formal legal query:

Whether the act of a person (hereinafter referred to as the 'Accused') who utilizes another individual's (hereinafter referred to as the 'Victim') identification documents to cast a vote in an election, constitutes an offence under BNS, specifically Section 121(a) of BNS - 'Fraudulent voting'?

Furthermore, under the provisions of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I seek clarification on the following:

1. Whether the action of the Accused amounts to a cognizable offence under BNSS?
2. What are the relevant procedures that the Election Commission or the competent authorities must follow in accordance with BNSS to investigate and prosecute this offence?

Additionally, the complainant seeks to invoke the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to initiate proceedings under Article 15(9) of BNSS to arrest the accused for commission of a cognizable offense and to direct the Station House Officer (SHO) to take immediate action under Article 19(3)(1) of BNSS against the accused.

Furthermore, it is requested that the incident be investigated under the provisions of BNSS, particularly Article 10(5) thereof, and that the evidence collected be recorded and preserved in accordance with the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

case_description: A drug dealer was caught selling narcotic substances near a school and was also found with a licensed firearm which he used to threaten buyers who owed him money.
rephrased_query:
**Petition under Section 123 (1) (a) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS)**

To the Hon'ble Magistrate,

A case of illicit trafficking and breach of public peace is reported to have occurred near a school premises. The accused, a known drug dealer, has been apprehended with evidence of narcotic substance possession and sale for consideration. Furthermore, during the investigation, a licensed firearm was discovered in the possession of the accused, allegedly used to intimidate buyers who were in arrears with payment.

**Inquiry under Section 59 (1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS)**

In light of the above circumstances, it is requested to initiate a preliminary investigation to determine the extent of the accused's involvement in the illicit trafficking of narcotic substances and to examine the circumstances surrounding the use of a licensed firearm in a manner contrary to its intended purpose.

**Admissibility of Evidence under Article 15 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA)**

Please determine the admissibility of the seized narcotic substances, licensed firearm, and any other relevant evidence in the trial of the accused, in compliance with the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA).

**Relief sought:**

a. Registration of an FIR (First Information Report) against the accused under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS).
b. Authorization of a preliminary investigation to gather further evidence.
c. Determination of the admissibility of the seized evidence in the trial of the accused.

Respectfully submitted,

[Your Name]
Petitioner.

case_description: During communal riots, a mob set fire to several houses and a member of the mob raped a woman whose family was fleeing.

case_description: A doctor at a government hospital demanded Rs 50,000 from a poor patient's family to perform an emergency surgery and refused to treat without payment.
rephrased_query:
Whether the conduct of the doctor constitutes an offence under Article 32 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023, specifically an act of "Commercial Bribery" whereby a public servant demands or receives gratification other than legal fees for the performance of a service, as mandated under Article 32(1)(d) of the BNS 2023, in contravention of Article 32(2) thereof, which prescribes that no public servant shall accept or receive gratification for any service other than legal fees.

Furthermore, the doctor's actions may also be examined under Article 53 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023, which deals with "Neglect of Duty" by a public servant, to determine whether his refusal to treat the patient without payment amounts to a wilful neglect of his duty as a medical professional, thereby violating his obligations under Article 53(1) of the BNSS 2023.

Additionally, the admissibility of evidence in this matter may be governed by the provisions of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023, specifically Article 27(1), which deals with the admissibility of statements made by a person in the presence of, or in response to, a public servant, in this case, the doctor, in the course of their official duty.

case_description: A woman mixed poison into her husband's food intending to kill him but he survived after being rushed to hospital; she was also found to have taken a large life insurance policy on him a week before.
rephrased_query:
**Petition for Investigation and Prosecution**

To the Hon'ble Magistrate under the provisions of Article 37 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS),

Pursuant to Section 167 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), I submit the following for consideration:

Whether the actions of a woman, who allegedly mixed poison into her husband's food with the intention to cause his death (contrary to Article 3 of BNS), and concurrently, procured a life insurance policy on her husband with the intent to gain financially from his demise, constitute the offence of 'Attempt to Murder' or other relevant provisions of BNS?

Whether the survivor's testimony, corroborated with medical evidence, and circumstantial evidence of the life insurance policy, are sufficient to establish a prima facie case against the woman for the above-mentioned offence(s)?

I request that a thorough investigation be conducted under the provisions of Section 156 of BNSS, and that the necessary steps be taken to prosecute the woman, if the evidence so warrants, under the provisions of BNS.

**Verification of Facts**

The petitioner requests that all relevant documents, including the life insurance policy, medical records, and testimony of witnesses, be produced and verified as per the provisions of Article 42 of BNS and Section 293 of BNSS.

**Prayer**

It is respectfully prayed that the Hon'ble Magistrate may take cognizance of the above-mentioned offence(s) and direct the Investigating Officer to proceed with the investigation, as per the provisions of Section 159 of BNSS.

**Verification and Certification**

This petition is verified and certified to be true to the best of the petitioner's knowledge by the undersigned.

**Signature of Petitioner**

However, due to timely medical intervention, he survived the ordeal. Furthermore, it has been discovered that she had taken out a large life insurance policy on her husband, a week prior to the incident, as per Article 123 of the BNS.

We request that an investigation be conducted under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS) to determine whether the wife's actions constituted a criminal offence, and if so, to identify the relevant sections of the BNS that have been contravened. We also request that the investigation gather evidence to establish the wife's motive and intent behind taking out the life insurance policy.

**Request for Evidence Collection:**

Pursuant to Article 50 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), we request that all evidence related to the incident, including medical records, witness statements, and insurance policy documents, be collected, preserved, and examined to determine their relevance to the investigation.

**Request for Proceedings:**

We request that the investigation be conducted in accordance with the provisions of the BNSS, and that the proceedings be recorded and preserved as per Article 75 of the BSA.

**Conclusion:**

We respectfully submit that the investigation and prosecution of this case are necessary to uphold the principles of justice and ensure that the law is enforced in accordance with the provisions of the BNS, BNSS, and BSA.

rephrased_query:
Pursuant to Article 3(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), we seek clarification on the applicability of the provisions governing 'assault' and 'outraging of modesty of a person', as defined in Chapter V, Section 2, 'Offences Against the Body', and Chapter VIII, Section 5, 'Offences Against Modesty', respectively, to the factual scenario wherein a group of men physically attacked and verbally abused a Dalit family in an act that appears to be motivated by casteism.

Furthermore, under the provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023 (BNS), Chapter X, Section 10, 'Criminal Conspiracy', we inquire about the potential applicability of this provision to the group of perpetrators, considering the concerted and premeditated nature of their actions.

Additionally, in light of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 (BNSS), Chapter V, Section 10, 'Protection of Victims and Witnesses', we seek guidance on the procedures to be followed in registering and investigating this incident, as well as the measures that can be taken to safeguard the Dalit family's rights and interests.

Finally, under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam 2023 (BSA), Chapter VII, Section 7, 'Relevant and Admissible Evidence', we request clarification on the admissibility of the casteist slurs uttered by the perpetrators as evidence of their intent and the potential for these to be considered as aggravating factors in the trial.
